title: Normalized resolution models of local hypercohomology
statement: For schemes $X,Y$ and $f:X\to Y$ [def-pc-scheme], use the sheaf-of-modules categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their supplied derived categories. The restricted coefficient map is the restriction-adjunction transpose of the original map followed by the target restriction unit, with the ordinary direct-image composition comparisons. The single-module cohomology comparison is homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso, with the supplied family of derived-category instances. The comparison $d_{f,K}:P^q_{f^{-1}(-)}(K)\simeq P^q_X(K)(f^{-1}(-))$ is topEdgeInverseModel, then exact precomposition homology, then the inverse of topEdgeLocalModel [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-top-edge]. For $F$ on $X$, an injective resolution $I$, an open $V$ of $Y$, $U=f^{-1}V$ (or an equal open), and restricted resolution data $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices], define $c_{f,F,V,I,R}:H^q(U,F|_U)\simeq P^q_Y(Rf_*F[0])(V)$ as follows. The resolution and exact forgetful comparisons followed by $H^q(R.sections)$ identify its source with cohomology of sections of $I$ on $U$. Extend by zero to integer indices and use exact evaluation. The inverse-open derived unit, evaluated on the integer-indexed injective resolution $I$, identifies this cohomology with inverse-open derived hypercohomology of $F[0]$. Follow its inverse by the inverse of topEdgeLocalLeray for $f$. This specifies actual isomorphisms with no arbitrary existence witness.

    (F : X.Modules) (q : ℕ) (V : Y.Opens) (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : U = f ⁻¹ᵁ V) (R : RestrictedResolutionSections I U) :

        ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology U.toScheme.toRingedSpace q).obj
          ((restrictFunctor U.ι).obj F)) ≅
      ((RingedSpace.localHypercohomologyPresheaf Y.toRingedSpace (q : ℤ)).obj

          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj F))).obj (op V)
